notes.title: Canonical ensemble
notes.summary: An equilibrium ensemble for fixed N, V, and T, obtained by coupling the system weakly to a thermal reservoir.
notes.content: The reservoir fixes temperature while energy fluctuates. The canonical probability distribution follows from equilibrium with a much larger bath.

notes.title: Partition function
notes.summary: The normalization factor that compresses the equilibrium state space into a single function.
notes.content: Derivatives of ln Z generate equilibrium moments and thermodynamic potentials.
assumptions: Discrete state notation shown; integrals replace sums for continua

notes.title: Helmholtz free energy from Z
notes.summary: The equilibrium Helmholtz free energy is determined directly by the canonical partition function.
notes.content: This relation makes Z a generator not only of averages but of the thermodynamic potential itself.

notes.title: Mean energy as a logarithmic derivative
notes.summary: The canonical mean energy is obtained from a logarithmic derivative of the partition function.
notes.content: Differentiating the Boltzmann weights brings down E_i and normalization converts the result into an average.
assumptions: Hamiltonian has no explicit beta dependence

notes.title: Energy fluctuation and heat capacity
notes.summary: Second derivatives of ln Z connect equilibrium fluctuations to a measurable response coefficient.
notes.content: This is a fluctuation–response relation in the canonical ensemble.

notes.title: Moment-generating function
notes.summary: A probability-theory object whose derivatives generate moments, structurally resembling the role of partition functions.
notes.content: The analogy is structural rather than an identity of physical interpretation.

notes.title: Grand partition function
notes.summary: The generating function for equilibrium systems with fluctuating particle number.
notes.content: Derivatives with respect to chemical potential generate particle-number statistics.
assumptions: Fixed T, V, and chemical potential

notes.title: Domain wall
notes.summary: A boundary separating regions with different local spin orientation.
notes.content: In one dimension, a domain wall costs finite energy but gains positional entropy.

notes.title: Why 1D Ising order fails at finite T
notes.summary: Finite-energy domain walls proliferate in a sufficiently long chain at any nonzero temperature.
notes.content: The density of walls is nonzero at finite temperature, so spin correlations decay over a finite correlation length.

notes.title: Cycle affinity
notes.summary: A signed measure of thermodynamic driving accumulated around a directed cycle.
notes.content: Nonzero cycle affinity obstructs detailed balance and encodes oriented circulation.

notes.title: Non-Hermitian spectral winding
notes.summary: A winding invariant describing how a complex spectrum encircles a reference point under a parameter cycle.
notes.content: Its exact thermodynamic meaning depends strongly on model class and parameterization.
assumptions: Point gap around the reference energy

notes.title: Detailed balance
notes.summary: A reversibility condition equating probability fluxes pairwise at stationarity.
notes.content: For connected finite networks it is equivalent to vanishing affinities on all independent cycles.

relations.label: normalization
relations.rationale: The canonical probabilities are normalized by Z.

relations.label: defines
relations.rationale: The canonical partition function determines the Helmholtz free energy through F = -k_B T ln Z.

relations.label: log derivative
relations.rationale: A beta derivative of ln Z gives the canonical average energy.

relations.label: second derivative
relations.rationale: A second beta derivative gives the variance and links it to heat capacity.

relations.label: generator structure
relations.rationale: Both encode a distribution in an exponential sum whose derivatives generate moments, while their physical meanings differ.

relations.label: sum over N
relations.rationale: Xi is built from canonical Z_N weighted by fugacity.

relations.label: destroys long-range order
relations.rationale: Finite-energy domain walls occur at nonzero density for any T>0 in the thermodynamic limit.

relations.label: equivalent criterion
relations.rationale: Detailed balance holds iff all cycle affinities vanish in a connected finite Markov network.

relations.label: possible orientation invariant
relations.rationale: Both quantities appear to encode directed circulation, but a general implication has not been established.
tests: Search for a counterexample with nonzero affinity but zero point-gap winding

relations.label: naive equivalence
relations.rationale: Detailed balance alone does not universally determine a chosen point-gap winding without specifying the operator family and reference point.
tests: Retain as a warning against overgeneralization
